title: Random forests, gradient boosting, XGBoost and LightGBM

videos.script: One tree on the churn data makes eight thousand reais. {{one}} A hundred trees, each fitted on a different resample, and averaged, make twenty-three thousand. {{hundred}} Nothing about the trees changed. Only how many were averaged. That is bagging. {{bagging}} Add a little more randomness, and it is a random forest. {{forest}} Boosting goes the other way. Small trees, one after another. Each one fitted to the mistakes of the trees before it. {{boosting}} Watch it on the deliveries. One tree is off by eleven minutes. A hundred are off by five, better than the line. {{curve}} Then the two libraries everybody uses for this, XGBoost and LightGBM. {{libraries}} And at the end, the honest question. Eight models, one table of reais. The jump from a line to trees is real. The differences among the tree ensembles are mostly noise. {{end}}
